gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-010 concerns omission of cone-description size from a running-time bound. It does not identify the separate failure that spectral normalization produces irrational data and that no rational, polynomial-bit reduction construction is proved.

Both entries identify the false assertion that every local minimum is Nash, and specifically the positive-valued local-minimum counterexample; both repair it by restricting the implication to nonpositive objective values.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The local-to-Nash implication fails for positive-valued local minima; only the nonpositive-valued case is justified.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claim that every local minimum is Nash is false because positive-valued local minima need not be blockwise globally minimizing.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states the Nash global-block obligation, gives a positive local minimum that is not Nash, and supplies the same nonpositive-objective qualification.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both discuss the proposition's construction involving V, but ISSUE-009 diagnoses division by zero and zero-eigenvalue block degeneracy. It does not recognize the distinct normalization defect in which an arbitrary scaled basis makes VV^T cease to be the orthogonal projector.

ISSUE-009 concerns undefined normalization when the spectral radius is zero. It does not identify the separate scaling error in the compressed spectral-radius identity for non-orthonormal U_G and U_H.

ISSUE-011 identifies the mismatch between ordinary AO convergence theory and extrapolated E-AO updates. It does not identify the distinct failure that the stated sphere-constrained block feasible sets are nonconvex, invalidating the convex-block premise.
